title: Kejriwal Detained Marching to Jantar Mantar, Posts Video: 'Youth Has Awakened'
excerpt: Delhi Police detained the AAP convenor outside his residence as he marched to Jantar Mantar for the CJP protest against CEC Gyanesh Kumar; hours later he posted a video declaring the country's youth has awakened.
body:
• NEW: Delhi Police detained AAP national convenor Arvind Kejriwal on Saturday outside his residence as he marched toward Jantar Mantar to join the protest against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. Hours later he shared a video on X declaring "the country's youth has awakened."
  • The march was part of the Cockroach Janta Party's "Save Democracy" protest demanding Kumar's resignation over alleged large-scale voter-roll deletions; police say more than 2,000 people were detained across Delhi on Saturday, including West Bengal Chief Minister Mamata Banerjee and CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke.
  • What it means for you: this is a fight over who gets to vote in India, not just a street protest. The Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls — which the opposition says has deleted around 130 million names — is the same administrative exercise that determines whether your family back home stays on the voter list.
  • Kejriwal was detained alongside AAP leaders Saurabh Bhardwaj and Sanjay Singh, a day after he urged young people to gather at Jantar Mantar in maximum numbers.

A Former Chief Minister Picked Up at His Doorstep

Delhi Police detained Aam Aadmi Party national convenor Arvind Kejriwal on Saturday while he was marching from his residence toward Jantar Mantar, where the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) had called a protest demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.

https://x.com/PTI_News/status/2108856331176497401

The former Delhi chief minister had spent the morning attacking the security clampdown in central Delhi as "worse than Emergency," and after CJP leaders were detained, he accused Prime Minister Narendra Modi of being "scared." On Friday, Kejriwal had said he and his family would attend the protest and urged youngsters to join the demonstration against what he called "vote theft."

Following his detention, Kejriwal shared a video on X with the caption "देश का युवा जाग चुका है" — "the country's youth has awakened." Senior AAP leader Atishi wrote: "Three-time Delhi Chief Minister Arvind Kejriwal brutally taken into custody by Delhi Police, for demanding Gyanesh Kumar's resignation. Modi Ji: how many people will you put behind bars to save Gyanesh Kumar?"

"Modi Ji: how many people will you put behind bars to save Gyanesh Kumar?"

— Atishi, AAP leader

Context & Background

The protest follows an Indian Express report that Kumar's own deputies questioned him over voter-list revisions that removed about 130 million voters. Opposition parties accuse the government of manipulating rolls through the Election Commission's Special Intensive Revision (SIR) exercise; the Election Commission and the BJP deny the allegations and call the revision standard administration.

Saturday's crackdown was sweeping: more than 2,000 people were detained across the capital, according to the Hindu BusinessLine. Mamata Banerjee was detained with five Trinamool Congress MPs on South Avenue. CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke, Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka were detained by police who boarded their Air India flight from Mumbai as it landed. YouTuber Dhruv Rathee was picked up at his Gurugram home, and AISA president Neha Bora, CPI(ML) Liberation's Dipankar Bhattacharya, Prashant Bhushan and Yogendra Yadav were detained near INA Market. Authorities shut 45 metro stations, suspended mobile internet in the central business district, imposed prohibitory orders, and barricaded central Delhi; markets including Khan Market and Connaught Place stayed shut.

Impact & Analysis

Kejriwal's detention changes the day's political weight. The earlier detentions of CJP's young leadership could be framed as routine protest management; picking up a three-time chief minister and sitting AAP convenor outside his own home is harder to contain as a law-and-order footnote. His video message, posted from detention, was aimed at one audience: the young voters he has been courting as the movement's engine.

The opposition's messaging has widened beyond Kumar. Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav said the resignation demand was now shared across opposition parties, while Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge accused the government of turning the "Mother of Democracy" into a "Muzzled Democracy." The BJP's Sambit Patra dismissed the stir as a "flop show."

For the diaspora, the underlying issue travels. The SIR revision is the administrative machinery that decides whose names appear on voter rolls — allegations of mass deletions, contested and denied by the Election Commission, strike at an instrument every Indian abroad expects to keep working for their family at home.

What's Next

The CJP has vowed to continue the protest despite the detention of its top leadership; one of its leaders, Ajinkya Shinde, urged people to keep marching toward Jantar Mantar, saying that wherever police stop them "will become your Jantar Mantar." The Indian Youth Congress has launched a legal helpline for detained protesters.

The deeper standoff is institutional: the opposition wants criminal charges against Kumar, a halt to the SIR exercise, and an independent process for choosing a new CEC — none of which a protest can deliver. Saturday's detentions are a chapter, not a conclusion.
